title: Unquoted expansion in command position is not word-split ($CC -c x.c with CC="cc -O2" → command not found)

labels.name: shell
labels.description: Parsing, quoting, expansion, pipelines, redirection, and shell execution

body:
An unquoted expansion used as the **command word** isn't word-split, so the whole value is looked up as one command name. Argument splitting works; only the command position is affected.

**Repro** (just-bash 3.4.2):

```js
import { Bash } from 'just-bash';
const r = await new Bash().exec('CC="echo cc -O2"; $CC -c x.c');
console.log(r.stdout, r.stderr);
```

- **Expected** (bash): `cc -O2 -c x.c`
- **Actual:** `bash: echo cc -O2: command not found`

The same happens with `set -- echo a b; $*` and with `X="echo a b"; $X`.

**Cause:** the simple-command executor expands `name` with the single-string expander, while the arguments go through the field-splitting one.

**Impact:** `$CC $CFLAGS -c file.c` is how Makefiles and configure scripts invoke compilers (e.g. zlib's configure runs `( $* )` inside backticks), so every such build fails with "command not found".

**Expected semantics:** split the name like arguments, run the first field, and prepend the remaining fields to the arguments. A quoted `"$X"` stays one word, and an empty expansion falls through to the next word, as in bash.

We carry a workaround hunk in [slicc's patch-package patch](https://github.com/ai-ecoverse/slicc/blob/feat/ladder-interop/patches/just-bash%2B3.4.2.patch). Happy to send a PR if useful.
